title: Site Finder v1
description: GB map, ranked answer, evidence for every site, pushback controls with a what-changed view, planning record by authority, and Gate 2 and headroom allocation.
why: Gives an origination team one place to ask where to build and see why, with the data behind every rank.

title: Ownership chain (v1.1)
description: Links the REPD applicant, the TEC and ECR capacity holder, the Ofgem generator, the LCCC CfD holder, the Companies House parent and HMLR company-owned land.
why: Shows who already holds consents, connections and land near a site, so a team can see competitors and likely sellers. Timing depends on a go-ahead.

title: Client accounts and single sign-on
description: Named accounts per customer and sign-in through the customer's own identity provider.
why: Lets a customer's whole team use the tool under their own security policy.

title: Scheduled data refresh
description: Rebuilds the data on a set schedule when publishers release new versions, and shows the build date on every screen.
why: Registers, headroom figures and the planning database change every quarter, and a stale shortlist misleads.

title: Per-site yield with P50 and P90
description: Replaces the regional yield layer with a per-site PVGIS calculation and a P50 and P90 range.
why: Yield feeds the price needed to hit the hurdle, and lenders and committees ask for P90.

title: CfD AR8 and AR9 eligibility screen
description: Flags whether a site's consent status and Gate 2 position fit the next allocation rounds.
why: Revenue route decides whether a site clears the hurdle, and the screen shows which sites could enter a round.

title: Battery storage siting
description: Ranks land for standalone and co-located batteries using headroom, planning precedent and flood risk.
why: Many teams now develop solar and storage together, and the same grid and planning data applies.

title: Planning applicant, agent and refusal reasons
description: Adds the applicant, the agent and the stated reasons for refusal from planning portals to each scheme in the planning record.
why: Refusal reasons show what an authority objects to, and the applicant shows who is active nearby.

title: Aerial imagery checks
description: Shows current aerial imagery beside each site and flags land use the open data cannot see.
why: Catches quarries, new housing and other features that the datasets lag behind.

title: Co-located solar at existing wind connections
description: Finds wind farms whose connection could take solar, using capacity, age and land around the site.
why: Reusing a connection can avoid a queue, which is often the longest part of a project.

title: Repowering candidates
description: Lists operating solar farms by age, connection capacity and land, as candidates for repowering or life extension.
why: Existing sites already have a connection and a consent.

title: Network-operator budget estimates and cable routing
description: Adds route-based cable costs and budget estimates from network operator charging statements in place of the cost table.
why: Connection cost is the largest uncertainty in the early numbers.

title: Onshore wind siting
description: Adds wind speed, noise buffers, radar and Scottish planning policy to the same ranked-site approach.
why: Teams with wind pipelines would use one tool across technologies.

title: Council political context
description: Adds council control and policy stance to the planning record where the data licence allows it.
why: Politics affects consent as much as policy does, but the data licence is unclear today.

title: Northern Ireland
description: Extends coverage to Northern Ireland using its own planning, grid and land datasets.
why: Some IPPs develop across the whole UK.
